backward_compat_traps.rule: The internal WCK must be phase-locked to CK via a WCK2CK synchronization (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR via CAS) before any high-speed read/write.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Omitting the WCK2CK sync (continuous-data-clock mindset) yields undefined read/write timing because WCK is otherwise disabled.

backward_compat_traps.rule: LPDDR5 has no CKE pin; low-power entry is a CA command that lasts until CS next goes high.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A controller expecting a CKE pin will not control LPDDR5 correctly.

backward_compat_traps.rule: In LPDDR5 the CAS command precedes the read/write and synchronizes WCK; it does NOT select a column.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating LPDDR5 CAS like LPDDR4's column-selecting CAS-2 produces wrong addressing/timing.

backward_compat_traps.rule: LPDDR4 C0-C9 are renamed in LPDDR5 to B0-B3 and C0-C5; writes start at a multiple-of-16 address (B0-B3 zero); reads may use a non-zero B3.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Reusing LPDDR4 column-bit naming mis-addresses the burst start.

backward_compat_traps.rule: LPDDR5 VDDQ is 0.5 V (vs 0.6 V LPDDR4X, 1.5 V DDR3).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Driving LPDDR5 IO at a higher VDDQ damages the device.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Exiting Deep Sleep Mode requires the full initialization sequence (ZQ + WCK2CK + training).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Resuming traffic immediately after deep-sleep exit without re-init is undefined.

fields.spec_version: JEDEC JESD209-5 — Low Power Double Data Rate 5 (LPDDR5) SDRAM Standard (19 February 2019), with addenda JESD209-5B (28 July 2021) and JESD209-5X (LPDDR5X).

spec_lineage_lpddr.summary: Original low-power DDR; 1.8 V; temperature-compensated / partial-array self-refresh; deep power-down.
1.2 V; 2n/4n prefetch + non-volatile option; 10-bit DDR CA bus; up to LPDDR2-1066.
1600 MT/s; write-leveling, CA training, optional ODT; 8n prefetch.
Two 16-bit channels; 6-bit CA bus (two-cycle commands, CS active-high, no CKE); 16n prefetch; DBI; up to 3200 MT/s. LPDDR4X reduces Vddq to 0.6 V.

WCK / RDQS on-demand clocking with quarter-speed CK; 7-bit DDR CA bus; 16 banks in 4 bank groups; 16n prefetch; VDDQ 0.5 V; link ECC; DVFS/DVFSC; deep sleep; Data-Copy / Write-X; CKE eliminated; up to 6400 Mbps.
Speed up to 8533 Mbit/s; tx/rx equalization; Adaptive Refresh Management.
Successor; CA bus narrowed further; 12-bit data bus per channel; higher speeds. Out of scope of JESD209-5.

previous_versions_of_this_spec.summary: LPDDR5/5X update: 8533 Mbit/s; tx/rx equalization; Adaptive Refresh Management.
LPDDR5X branded extension; later devices reach 8533+ Mbit/s on 14/12 nm-class processes.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: New clocking architecture: quarter-speed CK + on-demand full-speed WCK + DRAM-driven RDQS
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: WCK/RDQS enabled only when needed -> major IO power saving; requires WCK2CK sync before every high-speed transfer.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: CA bus widened to 7 bits, double data rate
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: Commands arrive at the same cadence as LPDDR4 despite quarter-speed CK; a command spans two CA transfers.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: CAS command moved before the read/write (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR)
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: CAS synchronizes WCK to CK (does not select a column), unlike LPDDR4's trailing CAS-2.
Bank-group timing enables concurrency; 16n prefetch retained (NOT doubled).
Lower IO power; DFE + (5B) tx/rx equalization required for SI.
On-the-wire single-bit correction; reduced driven-bit count.

key_changes_vs_lpddr4.change: DVFS / DVFSC, deep sleep, Data-Copy / Write-X
key_changes_vs_lpddr4.impact: Fine-grained power scaling and data-transfer reduction.
Low-power entry is a CA command bounded by CS.

fields.version_naming_history_note: LPDDR5 is the fifth generation of JEDEC's Low Power DDR SDRAM line (JC-42.6), standardized as JESD209-5 (19 February 2019). The LPDDR generational naming is separate from the mainstream DDR family. JESD209-5B (2021) added the LPDDR5/5X speed extension (8533 Mbit/s), tx/rx equalization, and Adaptive Refresh Management; JESD209-5X covers the LPDDR5X branding. LPDDR5 is distinguished from DDR3 (JESD79-3) by its WCK on-demand clocking, JESD209-5 numbering, mobile low-voltage operation (VDDQ=0.5 V), and CA-bus command encoding rather than separate RAS/CAS/WE pins.
